answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slow, public history resists sybils: each identity locks a modest bond and earns full weight only after weeks of verifiable work, like tending a garden where growth takes real time. A genuine record is singular, like one opal: it cannot be duplicated into many equally valuable stones. An attacker must fund, compute, and mature every fake identity separately, so cost scales linearly with each clone, while copied histories earn no extra weight — shale-like layers of duplicates are detected by provenance checks and forfeit their bonds.
